description: Ratchet on evidence, not on tests. audit-write-route-coverage.mjs asks whether a sensitive write route is tested and holds that at zero; this asks whether a write leaves the trail the rest of the system reconciles against, and both answers are currently backlogs rather than zeros. Neither list is a list of bugs: a company hard-delete that removes every inventory row, or a scheduler purging rows for a deleted stock item, has nothing to journal. The list is what a reviewer must look at when a file joins it. Both entries pin the set as well as the count, because a backlog that holds steady while a different file joins it is a new write path with no evidence wearing an old number. Re-pin downward with UPDATE_WRITE_EVIDENCE_BASELINE=1; the audit refuses upward.

stockWritesWithoutJournalEvidence.rationale: Files that move stock without going through postStockMovementTx, the only writer of the canonical stock movement journal. Stock moves two ways: a statement naming the inventory table, or a call to adjustInventory()/reverseInventoryByExactValue() in server/inventoryHelper.ts, which owns the balance arithmetic. The helper module itself is exempt — it is the layer the journal sits above and cannot know which document is calling it — but its callers are not. Convergence reconciliation compares stock documents against the journal, so a mutation missing from it is not a discrepancy the report finds; it is one the report cannot see.

teardown.reason: The inventory row is removed because the thing it belongs to is being erased — a company hard delete, a stock item purged from the deleted-items screen, an orphan sweep after a stock item is gone. There is no movement to record, and a journal row would be evidence pointing at a stock item that no longer exists.

revaluation.reason: Writes average_rate and total_value and never touches quantity. Nothing moved, so there is no movement to journal; convergence reconciliation compares quantities against the journal and would have nothing to compare a revaluation against.

reconstruction.reason: Recomputes the expected balance from the documents and writes that, rather than applying a movement. Journalling a correction as though it were a movement would report drift as physical stock. Both of these report every row they changed, which is the evidence they do leave.

migration.reason: One-off cutover paths that establish opening balances in a target company from a source company's closing stock. Arguably an opening balance is a movement from nothing and should be journalled; that is a genuine design question, recorded here rather than assumed either way.

identity-merge.reason: Collapses two stock-item identifiers into one, or undoes that: inventory rows are re-pointed at the kept item and their balances recombined. No stock physically moved, so there is no movement to journal — but the quantity attributed to an item does change, which is worth knowing when reading a convergence discrepancy against a merged item.

unjournalled.reason: Read and confirmed: each moves stock against a real document — a voucher, a transfer, a revision, an offload, an import — and leaves no journal row. These are the genuine backlog. The pattern across them is asymmetry: the paths that bring stock in were converted and the paths that take it back out were not. Stock transfer creation journals (server/storage/stock-ops/transfers-create.ts), and the lifecycle service that serves PUT /api/stock-transfers now journals its apply, unapply and posted-edit phases too; deletion journals the return, which is the only surviving account of it once the document is removed, and the immutable revision path journals its delta in the direction the stock travelled. Container offload execution journals (server/services/containers/offload-lifecycle/execute.ts) while create-correction, recalc and reverse do not. POS is the one symmetric family — deduct, edit-reverse and edit-rebuild all journal. So the journal records the issue and not the return, which is the shape most likely to make a convergence report look wrong when the data is right.

shadowed.reason: Write paths that cannot execute. Both register an Express route that an earlier registration already claims, and Express serves the first match: registerVoucherRoutes runs before registerFiscalTransferRoutes, and registerImmutableStockTransferRevisionRoutes before registerStockTransferRevisionLifecycleRoutes. Adding journal evidence here would be evidence written by code nothing calls; the real fix is deletion, which is a different change with a different risk. transfers-update.ts is only half dead — updateStockTransfer is unreachable, updateStockAdjustment is live and still owes evidence.

stockWritesWithoutJournalEvidence.reviewNote: Every file in `files` is classified under `reviewed`; `unreviewed` is empty and must stay that way. A file entering the backlog has to be read and classified, or fixed. `unreviewed` never means 'fine' — it means nobody has opened it.

voucherWritesWithoutRequestIdentity.rationale: Files that still create vouchers without a canonical stable posting identity. The retry need not be a user double-click: a proxy timeout, mobile network handover, or offline replay can submit the same operation again. A file is credited when it carries a stable request/source identity itself or reaches the central/infrastructure posting boundary that requires one. Phase 3 removed 11 infrastructure writers from the measured backlog by requiring deterministic source identity and serialized posting reuse. Phase 4 removes 22 high-risk operational writers by putting manual vouchers, payroll/advances, employee cash/POS and supplier payments behind a durable company-scoped request boundary whose stable identity survives browser retry/offline replay. The remaining active measured backlog is 48 creation paths: 15 explicit replay-guard paths, 11 migration/import/repair paths, and 22 Phase 5 operational paths. Only creation counts: updating, soft-deleting, restoring, or moving an existing voucher cannot produce a second voucher row.
voucherWritesWithoutRequestIdentity.reviewState: REVIEWED FILE BY FILE. The active 48 voucher creation paths are classified in config/voucher-write-evidence-review.json with zero unreviewed remainder. The 11 infrastructure writers completed in Phase 3 and the 22 operational writers completed in Phase 4 are retained separately in that review file and are forbidden from re-entering the measured backlog.
